# Job cards: numbering, status, billing and archiving, notes and assignees

> Detail split out of CLAUDE.md. Read before touching job numbering, job status, invoicing/archiving, deletion, comments or who is assigned.

## Numbering

**Job card auto-numbering**: Job numbers are auto-generated from two settings: `job_number_prefix` (e.g. `"DH-"`) and `job_number_next` (e.g. `"00001"`). The format preserves leading zeros (width of `job_number_next` string). On each job card creation, the server generates `{prefix}{paddedNumber}`, validates uniqueness, inserts the record, then increments `job_number_next`. Deleted job numbers are never reused. Numbers are compared without regard to case (Windows folders are case-insensitive, so `dh-0001` would share `DH-0001`'s folder); stored values keep the case typed. The prefix rule (letters, digits, `-`, `_`, up to 10) is judged only when the prefix actually changes, so a prefix saved before the rule existed does not block saving the other job-number settings. Settings refuses a starting number at or below the highest number actually handed out — the existing jobs plus deleted ones (read from the delete entries in the trail). The counter's own current value is not a floor, so a mistyped jump (e.g. 50000 for 00500) can be set back down. The job number field is read-only in the create form. Admin configures prefix and starting number in Settings > Job Card Numbering. If not configured, job card creation is blocked with an error message.

## The status list

**The list, its groups and who may set each status** live once in `server/src/shared/jobStatuses.json`, read by both sides. Sixteen statuses in six groups, in this order (which is also the sort order of every status column):

| Group | Statuses (code) | Set by | Left by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Quoting | To be Quoted (`TO_QUOTE`), Quote Sent (`QUOTE_SENT`) | management | management |
| Workshop | Open (`OPEN`), In Progress (`IN_PROGRESS`), Done (`DONE`) | everyone | everyone |
| On Hold | On Hold – PO / Material / Subcontract / Tools / Customer (`HOLD_PO`, `HOLD_MATERIAL`, `HOLD_SUBCONTRACT`, `HOLD_TOOLS`, `HOLD_CUSTOMER`) | everyone | everyone |
| Finishing | Ready to Collect / Deliver (`READY_TO_COLLECT`) | everyone | everyone |
| | To be Costed (`TO_COST`) | management | **admin** |
| | To be Invoiced (`TO_INVOICE`), Call for Payment (`CALL_FOR_PAYMENT`) | admin | admin |
| Closed | Paid – Archived (`ARCHIVED`, the `closedStatus`) | admin | unarchive only |
| Alert | Action Required (`ACTION_REQUIRED`, the `alertStatus`) | everyone | everyone |

"Admin" is the `invoiceJob` permission. The same file names the special codes once — `defaultStatus` (`OPEN`), `closedStatus`, `alertStatus`, `billedStatus` (`CALL_FOR_PAYMENT`), `billedStatuses` (Call for Payment + Paid – Archived, for Statistics' customer invoiced totals), `billingStatuses` (To be Invoiced, Call for Payment, Paid – Archived — the moves with billing checks, never a new job's status) and `settledStatuses` (Done, Ready to Collect, To be Costed, To be Invoiced, Call for Payment, Paid – Archived — never overdue, and a finish for Statistics).

**Status is only ever set by hand.** Nothing moves a job by itself — not starting or stopping a timer, not logging or deleting time, not adding, changing or removing a part, not a forgotten clock being cut. The work-driven automatic status (and `jobStatusAuto.js`) was removed on 2026-10-27: the office wanted the status to be what people say it is, and it removed a whole class of "the reply moved my status" races. No work route writes a `status` key into its trail entry any more and no part reply carries `jobStatus`; older trail entries still carry those folded moves and History still words them.

**The one-time rename.** The old list (Quote, Open, Material/Service, PO Requested, In Progress, Done, Customer notified, Invoiced) was folded onto the new one by `renameOldStatuses` in `legacyMigrations.js`, mapping in `db/statusRename.js` (pure, tested in `server/test/statusRename.test.js`): Quote → To be Quoted, Material/Service (and older Treatment / On Hold) → On Hold – Material, PO Requested → On Hold – PO, Customer notified → Ready to Collect / Deliver, Invoiced → Paid – Archived; Open, In Progress and Done kept their codes. It renames every job and every job trail entry's `status.from`/`status.to`, so past entries read in the new names and Statistics' settled-move query keeps matching. No flag: no current code reuses an old one. A boot that finds anything left to upgrade first saves `data/jobcard.before-status-change-<UTC>.db` (`db/safetyCopy.js`, `VACUUM INTO`, run from `schema.js` before the column drops); if that copy fails, both the rename and the quote-reference fold are held back for that boot. `DATA_VERSION` 11.

## Who can set status

**A move needs permission at both ends.** `canSetStatus({ canManage, canInvoice }, from, to, previous)` in `server/src/shared/jobStatus.js` allows a move when the actor meets the `leaveBy` level of where the job is **and** the `setBy` level of where it's going (a no-op is always allowed; a new job, `from` null, needs only the target end). So a worker can't pull a job out of Quote Sent or Call for Payment, and a manager can hand a job to To be Costed but never move it on (forwards or back) — only an admin does. `canChangeStatus(actor, current)` is the "is the control live at all" test (the actor meets `leaveBy` of the current status); `offeredStatusValues(actor, current, isEdit)` is the picker's rows (the current status plus every reachable one; never Paid – Archived while creating). An unknown code has no level and can be neither left nor set. `statusChangeRefusal` in `middleware/auth.js` is the role-to-booleans seam; its refusal says "Only an admin or manager can set that status." when a manager could have made the move, otherwise "Only an admin can move a job into or out of that status." It guards `PATCH /jobcards/:id/status`, `PUT /jobcards/:id` and — with `from` null — `POST /jobcards` (a manager can't create a job straight onto a billing status). **Action Required is a flag over the job's real status, not a side door**: taking a job off it also needs what leaving the status it remembers (`previous`) needs, so the office flagging a Call for Payment job never lets a worker move it on (`canChangeStatus(actor, current, previous)` and `offeredStatusValues(actor, current, isEdit, previous)` take the same argument; the server routes pass `existing.previous_status`).

**The drop-downs are grouped.** Both status pickers (job list badge, job screen pill) render `statusMenuModel` from `client/src/components/jobcard/constants.js`: the offered rows under their group headings (the headings are labels, not rows), drawn by one shared `common/StatusPopover.jsx`: opening it puts the keyboard on the current status, Up/Down/Home/End walk only the status rows, and it opens upward when there isn't room below inside whatever cuts it off (the list's scrolling table, or the window), with its height capped to the room it has, and, on a job sitting on Action Required that remembers where it was, a "Put back to …" row at the top when that move is allowed — under its own "Before the flag" heading on a tinted band, reading "↩ Put back to" then that status's own pill, with the keyboard placed on it when the menu opens so Enter puts the job straight back. The job list's filter row is All · Action Required (with a count of the jobs the list would show under All — "My jobs" and the search box applied) · Quoting · Workshop · On Hold · Finishing | Overdue (`ACTIVE_FILTER_OPTIONS` / `matchesStatusFilter`); single statuses are filtered on the Search page.

**Action Required remembers.** Moving into Action Required (or Paid – Archived) stores the status being left in `jobcards.previous_status`; leaving either clears it. Archiving a job while it is flagged keeps the status from *before* the flag, so unarchiving returns it there. It is bookkeeping, never in the trail. **A flagged job counts as the status it remembers** (`standingStatus` in `shared/jobStatus.js`): the overdue mark and Workshop Statistics' live, finished, overdue and invoiced figures read that, so flagging a finished job never turns it red or late. Its pill and badge show a rainbow running across the letters themselves (ink tokens `--status-alert-1…6`, both themes; the pill is left unfilled), a full sweep about every 2 seconds; the dots step through the same colours. Nothing blinks; reduced motion slows it to 8s rather than stopping it, like the spinner.

**Picking the status a job already has is not a change.** `PATCH /jobcards/:id/status` with the job's current status (a list or screen showing an older status — someone on another PC moved it) writes nothing, stamps no "Last Edited" and records no `from === to` trail entry; it answers with the job as it stands.

**"Last Edited" follows every edit, including the one-at-a-time ones.** Parts added/changed/removed (`jobcard-items.js`) and workers put on or taken off by management (`PUT`/`DELETE /jobcards/:id/assignees/:userId`) stamp `updated_by`/`updated_at` through `jobcardQueries.touch`, in the same transaction as the write, and only when something actually changed. Comments, files, prints and a worker's own self-assign do not count as edits of the job card and leave it alone.

## Billing and archiving

**Paid – Archived files the job away.** When a job moves to the `closedStatus` (via `PUT /:id` or `PATCH /:id/status`) the server sets `archived = 1` in the same `db.transaction` as the status write, so a failure between them can't leave a job reading Paid – Archived while still in the open list. Only an admin can set it. A job is never *created* on a billing status — `POST /` refuses To be Invoiced, Call for Payment and Paid – Archived with 400, and the create form never offers them — because only the update/status paths run the checks below and stamp the invoiced date. There is no manual archive endpoint; unarchive (`POST /:id/unarchive`, management) is the only way back. **An archived job is closed to every write, not just status**: one middleware, `closedJobGuard` (`server/src/middleware/closedJob.js`), is mounted once ahead of every `/api/jobcards/:id` route, so a route added later is closed by default too. It refuses any non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS request on an `archived === 1` job with 409 `{ error: 'This job is paid and archived. Unarchive it to make changes.', code: 'JOB_CLOSED' }` **before any write**. A short allow-list (one named constant in that file, a reason per entry) is let through anyway: unarchive, `DELETE /:id`, stopping a running timer, the print/packet previews, recording a print/save, and marking comments read. The lock keys off the `archived` flag alone. **Unarchive puts the job back where it was**: the status it had just before archiving (`previous_status`), or Call for Payment for a job archived before statuses were remembered (it had been billed). It keeps the invoiced date. The trail entry records `archived` and `status` from/to.

**The invoiced date is the day the bill went out.** `invoiced_date` is stamped the first time a job reaches Call for Payment (or goes straight to Paid – Archived without one), recorded in that move's trail entry, and never cleared — moving back, archiving and unarchiving all keep it. It is shown in the Excel job export and used as a finish-date fallback by Statistics.

**The billing statuses are admin-only (`invoiceJob`).** To be Invoiced, Call for Payment and Paid – Archived (and moving a job on from To be Costed) need the admin. Both status routes run `statusChangeRefusal` before `checkStatusMove`; the pickers hide what the person may not set through the shared `offeredStatusValues`.

**One shared status-move step for both routes**: `PUT /jobcards/:id` and `PATCH /jobcards/:id/status` run the exact same checks, in the same order, before any write, via one pair of functions in `jobcard-helpers.js`. `checkStatusMove(existing, newStatus, confirms, after)` returns a `refusal` (a `{ status, body }` the caller sends as-is) or a plan; `confirms` holds the "carry on anyway" flags from the body (`confirmMissingAttachments`, `confirmMissingInspection`, `confirmMissingPo`), and `after` is what the PO number and customer will be once this write lands (PUT can change the PO number in the same save). `applyStatusMove(move, userId, jobcardId)` is called from inside the caller's own write transaction after the status is written: it writes the remembered status and invoiced date (`setStatusBookkeeping`), files the job away when archiving, and returns the trail changes (`invoicedDate`, `archived`, `inspectionSignOff: '… archived anyway'`, `missingPo: { from: 'not entered', to: 'carried on anyway' }`) for the caller to fold into its own entry.

**Third soft checkpoint: a customer who needs a PO number.** A customer can be ticked "Customer requires PO#" (`companies.requires_po`, see `customers-and-tags.md`). A move into any `billingStatuses` status for such a customer while the job's PO number is blank answers 409 `{ error: 'MISSING_PO' }` before any write, unless the body carries `confirmMissingPo: true`. The client asks "No PO number — This customer needs a PO number for invoicing and none is entered. Carry on anyway?" (`confirmWithoutPo` in `jobCardPrompts.jsx`) and resends. Asked, never blocked: the PO may have come by phone or on paper. It is asked again on each later billing move while the box is still empty. The job screen waits for every save still on its way (`useSaveQueue.whenSettled`, passed to `changeJobStatus` as `beforeSend`) before sending the move, so a PO number typed a moment before picking the status is stored before it is judged. A saved job carries its customer's tick as `customerRequiresPo` (read live from the customer, management only), which drives the red note on the Customer Input card.

**The "are you sure?" is a server checkpoint too**, asked right after the hard blocks below and before the soft ones: on first reaching billing or on archiving, `checkStatusMove` answers 409 `CONFIRM_BILLING` (with `archiving`) until the body carries `confirmBilling: true`, so nobody answers the question for a move that was going to be refused.

**Hard running-timer checkpoint** (every billing move — To be Invoiced, Call for Payment and Paid – Archived — since a bill made on hours still moving is a wrong bill): `checkStatusMove` refuses **before any write**, and before the soft attachment checkpoint below, when any time entry on the job is still running (`end_time IS NULL`) — 409 `{ error: 'This job can\'t be billed or archived while a timer is running. Stop the timer first.' }`. Unlike the missing-attachments checkpoint this is a hard block with no confirm-anyway body flag: a running timer can't be confirmed away, since invoicing archives the job and an archived job's time can no longer be changed (see `docs/notes/time-and-costing.md`) — stopping it after the fact wouldn't be possible. The same hard refusal covers a **just-stopped block whose worker is still filling in the stop-timer form**: rather than guessing this from a blank description and a timing window (both of which a hand-added block could trip for innocent reasons), the block carries an explicit `awaiting_details` flag — set to 1 by the stop-timer route the moment it stops a block, and cleared to 0 only by the worker's own stop-timer form save (the form sends `detailsConfirmed: true`, which nothing else sends) or by resuming the block (clearing its finish time reopens it, so there's no pending form left to wait on). A manager editing the block's other fields — or the separate manual time-entry form — leaves the flag exactly as it was, so a manager's edit can no longer end the wait mid-form; a hand-added block never carries it, since only the stop route sets it. This is computed by the route (`PUT /:id/time-entries/:entryId`) and passed into `timeEntryQueries.update` as a parameter, not hard-coded in the query. A block on the job still marked `awaiting_details` and stopped — or, for a clock that stopped itself, answered (`finish_confirmed_at`) — within the last 30 minutes refuses the billing move with 409 `'Someone has just stopped a timer on this job and is still filling in their pieces. Try again once they have saved it.'` — otherwise archiving files the job away mid-form and the form's save is refused, losing the pieces, scrap and inspection answers. The 30-minute window means a form someone walked away from never blocks the job for good. Both checks live in one helper, `billingBlockedByTime` (`utils/timeEntryHelpers.js`), called from `checkStatusMove`.

**Hard unconfirmed-clock checkpoint**: checked right after the running-timer one (`billingBlockedByTime`, so every billing move too), also before any write and with no confirm-anyway flag: any time entry on the job still flagged `finish_unconfirmed` (a clock that stopped itself and whose worker has not said when they really finished) → 409 `{ error: 'This job can\'t be billed or archived yet because <Name> hasn\'t confirmed when their clock finished. Ask them to sign in and answer, or correct the time yourself.' }`, naming the first such worker. A management save of that row settles it. See `docs/notes/time-and-costing.md`.

**Soft close-out checkpoint**: When a job first reaches billing (from outside the billing statuses, whichever one it jumps to) or is archived, and any attachment gaps exist, `checkStatusMove` returns a refusal the caller sends as 409 `{ error: 'MISSING_ATTACHMENTS', attachmentWarnings }` **before any write**. The client shows an "Carry on anyway?" confirm and resends with `confirmMissingAttachments: true` in the body to bypass the check. **When the job declared files but the job-folders location can't be reached** (drive or network share offline), nothing is known about the files, so the checkpoint still stops before any write — 409 `{ error: 'FILES_UNREACHABLE', attachmentWarnings }` with `attachmentWarnings.filesUnreachable: true` — and `confirmFilesAnyway` asks "the job's files couldn't be checked … archive anyway?" instead of listing gaps; the same `confirmMissingAttachments: true` resend bypasses it. An unchecked job is never invoiced (and archived) silently. This is a soft nudge, not a hard block. Both routes always read the job's current, already-saved items for this check (parts are never part of either invoicing route's own body — see "Assignees" below) — `computeAttachmentWarnings` takes only `(jobcardId, items)`; the "no permanent id yet" skip inside it is dead-in-practice defensive code, not a caller-selectable option (the flag that used to select it was removed).

**Second soft close-out checkpoint: unanswered Critical sign-offs.** Right after the missing-attachments checkpoint, `checkStatusMove` also checks for finished runs that needed the Critical sign-off (`time_entries.critical_at_finish = 1` — decided per run, at the moment it finished; see `docs/notes/files-and-qa.md`) but are still missing one of the four inspection answers (`timeEntryQueries.getMissingInspectionByJobcard`). If any, and the caller hasn't already confirmed, it refuses 409 `{ error: 'MISSING_INSPECTION', inspectionWarnings: [{ id, workerName, startTime, endTime, itemNumber }] }` — a warning, not a hard block, since only an admin can bill anyway. The client's `confirmMissingAttachments` gets a sibling body flag, `confirmMissingInspection`, read the same way in both status routes; the job screen and the job list's status badge both handle either 409 in turn through the shared `changeJobStatus.js` (attachments first, then sign-off), each confirmed flag staying set on the resend so answering both questions sends both flags true. Carrying on folds `inspectionSignOff: { from: '<N> run(s) unanswered', to: 'archived anyway' }` (or `'billed anyway'` on the first billing move)` into the same trail entry as the archive (`applyStatusMove`). The job screen marks each such run "Sign-off missing" on its logged-work list, independent of whether it's actually invoiced.

**Both places that can move a job's status ask the exact same questions, worded once.** The job screen's status control (`JobIdentityStrip.jsx`) and the job list's status badge (`JobCardList.jsx`'s `handleQuickStatusChange`) both go through `changeJobStatus.js`, which first waits for the caller's pending saves (`beforeSend`), then on a billing move runs the caller's pricing check (`prepareBilling` — the job screen refuses a red pricing box and saves unsaved pricing first; only it can fetch a fresh total) and sends the move; the server's hard blocks (running timer, unconfirmed clock, a stop form still being filled in) answer first, and only then does it ask back with 409 `{ error: 'CONFIRM_BILLING', archiving }` — the client fetches the fresh total at that moment and asks `confirmStartBilling` on first reaching billing ("Move job <number> to To be Invoiced?" — "Check the total is what the customer will be billed.") or `confirmMarkArchived` before Paid – Archived ("Mark job <number> paid and archive it?" — "It will be locked and moved to the archive. Unarchive it if it ever needs editing again.", buttons "Go back" / "Archive and lock"; the job screen alone passes a freshly-fetched total and whether costing was just saved, since only it has costing access), then answers each soft checkpoint in turn from one `CHECKPOINTS` table — files (`confirmFilesAnyway`), sign-off (`confirmWithoutSignOff`), PO (`confirmWithoutPo`) — resending with every answered flag kept set.

**The client has one rule for "is this job closed?"**: `isJobClosed(job)` in `client/src/utils/jobLock.js` reads the same `archived` flag the server's `closedJobGuard` keys on, and nothing in the client tests `status === 'INVOICED'` or the job list's "Show Archived" view toggle to decide whether a job can still be changed any more — both used to be used as proxies and could disagree with the row actually being closed (a manager viewing a closed job through search, or a stale `status` field, isn't necessarily archived, and the toggle says nothing about any one row on screen). The job screen's loaded job carries `archived` through into its form state (`mappers.js`'s `getDefaultFormData`, `useJobCardForm.js`'s `setFormDataFromJobCard`) — left out of the unsaved-edits snapshot the same way `status` is, since it's server-driven, never typed. On a closed job, `JobCardModal.jsx` shows one line at the top ("This job is invoiced and closed. Unarchive it to make changes.") and wraps the editable part of the Details tab's management view (fields, parts, workers — the comments lock themselves and stay outside, so their Retry still works) and of the Costing tab (the sheet body — `CostingTab`'s `locked` prop; its header's "what this job used" toggle and the load-failure Try again stay outside) each in a plain `<fieldset disabled>` (`.jc-lock-fieldset` in `JobCardModal.css` strips its default box so it doesn't disturb the layout) — this refuses interaction with every input, select, textarea and button inside it, for every role, without threading a lock prop through each one; the worker view is already fully read-only regardless. The per-item file-attach button and the timer Start/Stop buttons are hidden outright rather than left disabled, since a closed job can never have a timer running against it (invoicing is refused while one is) — there's nothing left to stop. **A write that reaches the server anyway** (the job was invoiced and archived from another PC while this screen still had it open) comes back with the 409/`JOB_CLOSED` shape above; the save queue (`useSaveQueue.js`, covering every field/part/worker write), the status control (`JobIdentityStrip.jsx`), comments (`useJobNotes.js`), manual time entries (`useTimeEntries.js`), the pricing sheet (`useCostingSave.js`, which also drops its unstored figures), timer start and the stop form's save/resume on this job (`useTimer.js` — which also closes the stop form when its save or resume is refused because the job was closed or the block deleted, since that form has no Escape and neither button could ever work again), and file uploads, re-tags and deletes (`useJobFiles.js`, via `JobPaperworkHub.jsx`'s `onJobClosed`) all recognise it (`jobLock.js`'s `isJobClosedError`) and call one shared handler (`JobCardModal.jsx`'s `handleJobClosedWrite`) instead of their ordinary failure toast — it shows the same sentence with a stable id and reloads the job, so the screen catches up and goes read-only. Timer stop itself is allow-listed through the lock, so it never meets this refusal; the "stop & switch" start is still not wired (it is safely refused server-side with its own error). The status control's own invoicing is the one close that comes from this screen rather than elsewhere: `changeJobStatus.js` hands the status reply to its caller, and `JobIdentityStrip.jsx` reloads the job when that reply says the job is archived, so the screen locks at once. The header strip (priority, description, due date, status) sits outside the lock fieldsets, so it checks `isJobClosed` itself and shows plain text on a closed job. Inside the Details lock, a finished run's view-only "Inspection" expander is still disabled on a closed job (it sits inside the parts list, which is locked as one piece).

## Deleting a job

**Soft delete checkpoint**: `DELETE /jobcards/:id` (admin) never deletes on the first request — because deleting is permanent and the job number is never reused, the server always returns 409 `{ error: 'CONFIRM_DELETE', workWarning }` **before any write** unless the body carries `confirmDelete: true`. `workWarning` is `null` when the job has no recorded work (client shows a plain "are you sure"); when any time has been logged or a timer is running (both cascade away on delete) it carries `{ hasActive, activeWorkers, loggedHours, pastWorkers }` so the confirm can name who/what is being erased. The confirmation lives entirely in this one 409 round-trip — there is no separate client-side pre-confirm — so the admin only ever sees a single dialog. Resending with `confirmDelete: true` bypasses the gate. Mirrors the missing-attachments checkpoint.

## Comments (notes)

Notes endpoints: `GET /jobcards/:id/notes` (authenticated — **newest first**, `created_at DESC` with `rowid` as tie-break), `POST /jobcards/:id/notes` (authenticated), `DELETE /jobcards/:id/notes/:noteId` (management), `PUT /jobcards/:id/notes/read` (authenticated, body `{ seenUpTo }`; see unread below). The **job list response also carries each job's newest comment** as `latestNote` (`{ text, userName, createdAt }`, or `null`) — fetched for all listed jobs in one pass by `getLatestNotesForJobcards` (`db/queries/operations.js`, a `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY jobcard_id ORDER BY created_at DESC, rowid DESC)` pick, i.e. **the same ordering the thread uses**, so the column can never show a different comment than the top of the thread when two share a timestamp; it returns raw rows and the route converts to camelCase at the boundary) and rendered as the **Latest Comment** column sitting between Status and Priority in the job list (full text floats on hover with author + time). Adding or deleting a comment in the job screen hands the newest remaining comment back to the list via `onNotesChange`, which **patches that one row in place** (never a whole-list re-fetch). It comes straight from the write's own reply — the new comment from the add, `latestNote` (same ordering as the thread) from the delete — so the row updates even if the window closed meanwhile, and the thread is re-read only while the window is still open. The column ids `latestNote` and `print` must each exist in **both** `DEFAULT_COLUMN_ORDER` (`JobCardList.constants.js`) and its server mirror `JOBCARD_COLUMN_IDS` (`middleware/validation.js`) — the server validates saved column order/visibility against that list, so a column missing there breaks reordering for everyone. The **Print** column reads `printedAt` straight off each job in the list response (stamped by the print-confirmation route once a packet carrying the job card has actually reached a viewer — see `docs/notes/files-and-qa.md`) and sorts via a getter in `useJobCardSort.js`, the same pattern every sortable column follows. `mergeColumnOrder` folds a newly-added column into a user's saved order at its default position and always keeps `actions` last. The Excel export re-reverses the thread so its Notes cell still reads oldest-first.

**Comments live in their own window, not in the Details tab.** On an existing job, every role and every tab, a round chat bubble (with a red count of *new* comments, nothing when there are none) floats just outside the job window's top-left edge. Pressing it slides a 360px comments window open to the left of the job (`JobCommentsPanel.jsx`, handed to `BottomSheet` as its `aside`): the job window keeps its size and the comments hang outside its left edge. To make room the pair slides right just far enough for the comments to fit in the left margin (never pushing the job off the right of the screen); when the screen is too narrow for both, the comments overlap the job's left edge instead. The slide is a margin, not a transform, because a transform would become the anchor for every fixed-position pop-up inside the job window. It reads like a chat: oldest at the top, the signed-in person's own comments on the right in the accent colour, everyone else's on the left with initials and name, day separators, and comments by one person within five minutes grouped. Enter sends, Shift+Enter is a new line. Escape pressed inside the comments window closes only that window (it marks the key handled, so the job window's own Escape stands down); the row holding both windows is the job window's Tab trap, so focus can move between them. Whether the window is open is decided afresh each time the job is opened (see unread below); nothing is remembered in the browser. Deleting a comment is management-only (a trash icon shown on hover, with the usual confirm). On an invoiced (closed) job the typing box and delete are replaced by a line saying to unarchive first. An unposted comment still counts as unsaved work when the job is closed — and so does one still sending (its text has already left the box): closing waits for it alongside the job's own saves, up to the same few seconds; a failed send puts the draft back and the usual unposted-comment question follows, one still on its way after the limit is named as "Your comment is still being sent", and a refresh while it sends gets the browser's leave-page question.

**The side windows close with an X (Comments and History alike), and the History count follows its filter.** The close control is a drawn X with the tooltip "Close"; the comment Send button's tooltip is "Send". In the History window, with any kind chip switched off the line under the title reads "3 of 12 changes" (shown of all) instead of the full count. Plain click on a chip still hides or shows that kind; **Shift+click shows only that kind**, and clicking the one kind left showing brings every kind back (hiding it would leave nothing).

**Unread comments, per person.** A comment is *unread* for a person when someone else wrote it and it is newer than the moment that person last saw the job's comments. Their own comments are never unread. It is stored on the server per person per job (table `job_note_reads`: `user_id`, `jobcard_id`, `seen_up_to` = the `created_at` of the newest comment seen; cascades with the job) because workers share PCs. A person's effective "seen up to" is the greatest of their own row, the launch baseline (setting `comments_read_from`, stamped once with the current moment by a startup conversion in `legacyMigrations.js` only when absent, so comments that existed before the feature don't all arrive as unread; a restored older backup gets it stamped by the same conversion pass) and their account's `created_at` (a new worker inherits no backlog). That rule is written once, as `SEEN_UP_TO_SQL` in `db/queries/operations.js`, and used by both the single-job value and the list count. `GET /jobcards/:id` carries `commentsSeenUpTo` for the signed-in person; the job list carries `unreadNotes` per job (one query for all listed ids, `getUnreadNoteCountsForJobcards`). `PUT /jobcards/:id/notes/read` takes `{ seenUpTo }` (any ISO-8601 moment, rewritten to the stored milliseconds-and-Z shape before anything compares it as text), clamps it to the newest comment actually on the job, only ever moves the mark forward, and returns `{ commentsSeenUpTo, unreadNotes }` (the person's unread count for that job afterwards, from the same counting as the list); the effective "seen up to" falls back to the 1970 moment when none of the three exist, never an empty string; it is allowed on a closed job (listed in `ALLOWED_ON_CLOSED_JOB`) and writes no trail entry. On screen: once both the job and the first read of the thread have arrived, the comments window opens by itself if anything is unread and stays closed otherwise — decided once per opening (each opening is a fresh job window, so the decision is made on that opening's own thread and read mark, never on the previous one's), never again, and without moving focus off the job (focus moves only when the person presses the bubble or the close button). Whenever the window is open and the newest comment is newer than the mark (including the person's own just-posted comment), the screen sends the read call and takes the reply as the new mark; a failure is silent and retried the next time the window is opened, never in a loop. Pressing the bubble re-reads the thread first, so a comment posted from another PC shows up and is counted as read. A thin "New" line sits above the first comment that was unread when the job was opened (worked out once per opening, kept until the job closes). The header line reads "J-2417, 5 comments, 2 new". In the job list, a job with unread comments shows a small accent dot before its Latest Comment and the text in bold, titled "2 new comments"; reading the thread sets that row to the returned count in place (`onCommentsRead`), and it still does when the window was closed before the reply arrived, because the call names its job; the finish-question's own job window passes it too (it reloads the list), the search page doesn't because its results carry no unread mark.

**Mentions.** A comment can @mention staff. `POST /jobcards/:id/notes` takes an optional `mentionUserIds` (an array of at most 20 non-empty strings; anything else is a 400). The route drops repeats and the writer's own id (mentioning yourself is ignored silently); every other id must be an existing **active** person, or the whole post is refused with a 400 whose `fields` marks the text box (the validator's own refusals — too many ids, not a list, bad entries — are reported under `text` as well, via `FIELD_ALIASES` in `validation.js`, so every mention refusal marks the same box) — the comment box shows it under itself while the job window is up, and it is a pop-up naming the job only if the window has closed. An archived person gets "<Name> can no longer be mentioned — their account is archived." with `code: 'MENTION_INACTIVE'`, which the client branches on; an id that names nobody at all (unknown, or with stray spaces) is a garbled request and gets the validator's "Couldn’t tell who was asked — pick them again from the @ list." with no code. Each mention is its own `job_note_mentions` row (`note_id`, `jobcard_id`, `user_id`, `mentioned_name` = their name or username as it reads after the @, `created_at` = the comment's, `answered_at`); the 201 reply carries `mentions: [{ userId, name }]`, and the comment's trail entry carries a `mentioned` field (`from: null`, `to: 'Name One, Name Two'`). `GET /jobcards/:id/notes` gives every comment a `mentions` array (empty when none), from one extra read for the whole job. **The answer rule:** a mention is *open* until the mentioned person posts any comment on that same job after it; that one comment answers **all** their open mentions on the job, in the same transaction as the post. `GET /jobcards/open-mentions` (any role, registered ahead of the `/:id` routes in `jobcard-notes.js`; a GET is never stopped by the closed-job lock) returns the caller's open mentions grouped per job, oldest waiting first: `{ jobcardId, jobNumber, description, count, firstNoteId, oldestAt, firstText, askers }` (the `first*` fields describe the oldest open mention's comment — the one the row opens at, so what the row shows, its time and where it lands all agree; `askers` is every distinct asker (by account, so two people sharing a name are two) of that person's open mentions on the job as `[{ userId, name }]`, the name being the asker's current display name (the comment's stored name if the account is gone), ordered by when each first asked — the row reads "Alice asked you", "Alice and Bob asked you" or "Alice, Bob and N others asked you", with the first asker's initials and a "+N" badge when there are several). `GET /auth/me` carries `openMentions: { count, signature }` (`signature` is built from one cheap summary of what is waiting — how many, the newest mention's time and the sorted ids of the visible jobs holding them — so a mention added or answered, or a job archived or unarchived (the id list changes, so even one archived while another is unarchived), shows without a second request; an ordinary edit to one of those jobs does not change it; `null` if that read failed). **Open mentions on invoiced (archived) jobs are left out of the list and the count** — nothing can be posted there to answer them — and they return if the job is unarchived. Backups before data version 9 restore the table empty. **On screen: the "Needs your attention" window.** `context/FinishQuestionProvider.jsx` (which composes the clock question and the mentions into the one window; the mentions side — list, row-opened job, re-read, held flag — is `hooks/useMentionAttention.js`) reads the list at sign-in, whenever the `/auth/me` poll reports a new `openMentions.signature` (`AuthContext` writes it into the small store in `context/openMentionsMarker.js`, which `FinishQuestionProvider` watches; `hooks/useOpenMentions.js` does the read, newest read wins, a failed read keeps the old list and forgets the marker, so the next poll that gets through reads again even when nothing changed — the retry rides the poll, never a loop of its own) and after a job opened from a row closes. The mentions are the "Questions for you" section of `common/AttentionDialog.jsx` (the same blocking window that carries the forgotten-clock question): a heading counted in questions, not jobs ("Someone asked you a question" for one; "You have N questions" when they are all on one job; "You have N questions on M jobs" otherwise — one job can hold several questions from different people), an instruction line ("Open each one and reply. Any reply counts, and this window closes once they're all answered."), then one button row per job, led by who asked and what: the asker's initials circle (the comments window's colours), "<name> asked you · <time>" (time if today, else short date; "· N questions" when more than one), the oldest open question's text (up to two lines), then the job number and description in small print, and an arrow as the open cue. The window has a plain border (the forgotten-clock section carries its own warning icon), and the footer reads "Can't deal with this now?" beside Sign out. An @name counts only as a whole word: a person answers to their full display name and, when it has more than one word, to its first word too ("@Sam" for "Sam Smith"). The text after the @ must be that name (capitals ignored), followed by the end or something that is not a letter or digit, and the longest name wins ("@Jo Bloggs" never also mentions Jo; "@Joanne" never highlights "@Jo"). A matched name belongs to the people whose FULL name it is; only if there are none, to the people whose first name it is. One person: them. Several: the one picked from the @ list, else the name is *unclear* (never silently nobody). The one rule, and the one lookup built from the staff list (lower-cased name -> `{ display, full, first }`), is `components/jobcard/mentionNames.js`, used for who a sent comment mentions, for the live "Will ask" line and for highlighting (a shown comment is searched against the same lookup built (`buildNameLookup`) from the whole staff list plus every person the thread's comments mention (`mentionedPeople`) — one lookup per thread, so someone since archived still reads whole; which names count as stored mentions is `storedMentionsByName`, also in `mentionNames.js`, not a second copy in the panel; sending still uses the active staff only — longest name first, and only a name that is one of its stored mentions is highlighted — so with Sam Smith stored, "@Sam Jones" is read as the whole name Sam Jones and nothing is highlighted; a first word like "@Sam" is highlighted as a stored person only when sending would have read it as them — nobody's whole name is "Sam" and, the writer aside, they are the only Sam in that same name set — so an unclear "@Sam" sent with "Send without asking them" is never coloured as the Sam who was mentioned by full name). **The writer is never a match for an @name**: the lookup is built from the whole staff list, the writer included, so where a name ends is read the same for everyone ("@Sam Jones" written by Sam Jones is that whole name, never "@Sam" plus a surname that would ask Sam Smith), and the writer is then left out of who it means (`resolveMentions`, the same rule as the @ list): an @name that only fits the writer asks nobody, and a first name shared with the writer is not "which one?". The writer's name counts as known for the "Nobody here is called…" check, so a self-mention posts quietly with no confirm. Who a comment mentions is worked out from its finished text against the active staff list when it is sent, so a name typed out by hand counts the same as one picked from the @ list. **Picks** (people chosen from the @ list) only settle a name that several people share; a pick counts only while that name is still in the text, and all picks are forgotten whenever the box becomes empty by any route (typing, deleting, sending — one place, the setter the panel uses). **Nothing is sent without the writer knowing who will be asked**: under the box, whenever the draft mentions anyone, the hint reads "Will ask: Jo Bloggs, Sam Smith" (full names, the writer left out; an unclear name shows as "Chris (which one?)"), worked out live by the same rule as sending, so a typo like "@Jo Blogs" visibly asks Jo. **An @word that names nobody, or a shared name with no pick, is never sent silently**: before posting, the staff list is fetched again (the window's copy may be empty or stale) — only when some such word has not already been checked against a fresh list in this window — and, if a word still matches nobody (`findUnmatchedMentions`), the writer is asked "Nobody here is called “Bob”, so nobody will be asked. Send anyway?" (Send anyway / Keep editing); a name with several people and no pick is asked as 'There is more than one person called “Chris” — pick the one you mean from the @ list. Send without asking them?' (Send without asking them / Keep editing); both in one comment is one confirm covering both. Only a word starting with a letter counts as a tried name ("@3pm", "@12" are ignored). A comment naming more than 20 people is stopped before sending and the comment box says "A comment can ask at most 20 people." (`MAX_MENTIONS`, `server/src/shared/mentions.js`, also the route's limit). **Sending is chat-style** (a send or delete moves through one stage in `useJobNotes.js` — idle, checking, sending or deleting, back to idle in a single `finally`; anything but idle gates Send, Enter and the delete buttons, "sending" alone is what close treats as a comment still on its way, and the stage is let go before the thread is re-read; the thread's own "loading" flag only means the thread is being read). **The checks can be cancelled**: after each wait in them (the fresh staff list, the "Send anyway?" question) the send carries on only if the job window is still up and the box still holds exactly the checked text; if the person closed the job meanwhile (and agreed to lose the unposted comment) or changed the text, it stops quietly and posts nothing. Deleting a comment is refused (with the "Still sending a comment" pop-up) before its "Delete?" question when a send is busy. While the checks run the box is read-only (so the text checked is the text sent), the @ list stays shut and picks are ignored; once they pass the sent text leaves the box and the picks are cleared at once, before the save. If the save fails the draft comes back (in front of anything typed meanwhile, separated by a new line) with its picks, and the refusal marks the box as before. Only a refusal coded `MENTION_INACTIVE` (a person archived meanwhile) reads the staff list again so they drop off the @ list; other failures do not. Two staff whose names differ only by capitals are told apart by the person picked from the list. **While the @ list is open, Enter never sends**: with a name highlighted it takes it; with nothing highlighted it closes the list (as Escape does) and the next Enter sends — a half-typed "@Jo" can't go out by accident (a worker can't delete their own comment). With no mention in the draft the hint under the box reads "Type @ to ask someone · Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line". Posting any comment on a job, from any job window, takes that job's row off the list at once (the post answered it) and then reads the list again only when there is something to settle: a row was showing for that job, or a read is already on its way (it may carry a question for that job that the post has just answered, and only a newer read can throw it away). Otherwise the next `/auth/me` poll covers it — a question asked since the last read and then answered by this post changes the signature, which brings its own read. Sign-in makes one read: the login sets the marker before the person, so the list is read once the person is known, with the marker already there. Only the newest read is ever applied, so a read already on its way — possibly made before the reply was saved — is thrown away instead of bringing the answered row back. Pressing a row opens that job in the provider's own job window with its comments open, scrolled to the oldest open mention, cursor in the reply box; the attention window is hidden meanwhile and, on close, the list is read again — the row is gone if the person replied, still there if not. Because closing waits for a reply still sending (see above), that read leaves only after the reply has saved. Everyone gets it, admins included. **It waits until no other window is open** (the shared modal stack, `common/modalStack.js`, says so): a person typing on a job screen is not interrupted and gets it the moment they close that window, while someone with nothing open gets it straight away; once the mentions are up they stay up (that holds for the mentions section itself — a clock question opening over a job screen never lets the rows in behind it), and they are hidden while a stop form is showing, while a check for owed stop forms is still running (at sign-in, after the clock is answered, after a stop form closes — if the mentions are already up they stay up, greyed out, until the check ends, so the window never closes and reopens), and after a job opened from a row closes until the list has been read again (a read overtaken by a newer one only counts as done once the newest has landed), so an answered row never flashes back. **The clock section is the exception**: a flagged clock shows over everything, as before, and while it shows every mention row is greyed out with "Answer your clock first." (while only the owed-stop-form check holds them, the note reads "One moment…"). What the window shows — clock, greyed or pressable rows, the reason — is decided in one place, `decideAttention` in `context/attentionDue.js`; nothing else re-derives it. **The cursor is never put on Sign out**: when the content changes, focus already on an answer control stays; otherwise it goes to the first pressable control in the sections, or to the window itself if none is pressable yet, and moves to the first row the moment the rows become pressable. The order when several are owed: the clock question, then owed stop forms, then mentions. The only way out besides answering is the **Sign out** button in the footer (no close button, Escape does nothing; when a screen behind holds unsaved work, e.g. a new job being typed, it first asks "Sign out? You have an unsaved job card. Signing out now will lose it." with Sign out / Stay signed in); the window goes away by itself once nothing is left.

## Assignees

**A worker can't be taken off a job while their clock is running on it** — by themselves or by the office (409), or the job would show nobody on it while time is being logged. Stop the clock first.

Assignee endpoints: `PUT /jobcards/:id` no longer takes `assigneeIds` at all — the branch that reconciled a whole list was stripped in Stage 4b of `tasks/instant-save-job-card.md` once nothing sent it any more (the job screen writes one worker at a time, and `buildJobcardPayload` only puts `assigneeIds` in the **create** payload). `POST /jobcards/:id/assignees/self` (authenticated, idempotent self-assign — uses `req.user.userId`, body ignored), `DELETE /jobcards/:id/assignees/self` (authenticated, idempotent self-unassign). Self routes log history with action `self_assign` / `self_unassign`. `PUT /jobcards/:id/assignees/:userId` and `DELETE /jobcards/:id/assignees/:userId` (both management, idempotent, 404 if the user doesn't exist) put or take off **one** worker without touching anyone else's row — the instant-save equivalent of the self routes, for the person ticking names on someone else's behalf. History action `assign` / `unassign`. **Every one of these four entries (and the timer's auto-assignment through `autoAssignWorker`) changes exactly one person, and names them in its snapshot as `{ workerId, workerName }`** (the shared display-name rule); the job History window words "put Ben on the job" / "took Ben off the job" from that alone and never splits or compares the joined `assignees` lists, so two staff with one name or a name with a comma read right. Older entries get `workerName` from the once-only History conversion (rules in `server/src/db/trailEntries.js`, applied by `legacyMigrations.js`; assign and unassign entries only, never self-assign) only when the joined lists give one exact answer. Both keep the same `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE` swallow the self routes use, since a timer auto-assigning the same worker can race the same insert. These are what the job screen's people tiles now call on every tap. **All four routes are refused on an archived (invoiced) job** by `closedJobGuard` (see "Invoicing and archiving" above) before the route itself ever runs, with `409 { error: 'This job is invoiced and closed. Unarchive it to make changes.', code: 'JOB_CLOSED' }`; the job list's Assigned To column and the job screen's people controls go read-only on such a job the same way the status badge already does, so the refusal is normally never hit from the screen.

Item endpoints, same instant-save batch (`server/src/routes/jobcard-items.js`, management, wired into the job screen's parts list via `useInstantItems.js`): `POST /jobcards/:id/items` adds one part (closed by `closedJobGuard` like every other write on an archived job — see "Invoicing and archiving" above); `PATCH /jobcards/:id/items/:itemId` changes one part — absent fields are unchanged, the body is merged over the stored row before validating, and the part never moves position; `DELETE /jobcards/:id/items/:itemId` removes one part (blocked if time is logged against it, or if it's the job's last remaining line). All three run the same seven item validators the create route (`POST /jobcards`) uses, grandfathering values already saved elsewhere on the job, and each names the part in its error message by description rather than position (a one-element validation batch can't report a meaningful array index) — `PUT /jobcards/:id` no longer takes `items` either, so these are now the *only* way an existing job's parts change. **A part's `item_number` is a sort order the server owns, not its identity — its permanent `item:` id is.** A new part gets `MAX(item_number) + 1` for the job, computed inside the same transaction as its insert, so it can never collide with a number picked at the same moment or repeat a gap. **Nothing renumbers on delete** — gaps are expected and fine; the number shown on screen is the part's `position`, a display-only field the **server** states on every part it returns — its 1-based index in that job's parts ordered by `item_number` ascending. A screen never counts this for itself any more (it used to, per-screen, before this field existed) and never sends `position` anywhere or writes it onto a row — identity is always the permanent `item:` id. A one-time startup conversion (`cleanUpDuplicateItemNumbering` in `db/legacyMigrations.js`) folds any job whose numbers still carry **duplicates** from before this change onto a clean 1..n ordering; gaps are left exactly as they are, since closing them on every boot is the very instability this change removed. It runs on every boot and is a no-op once a job has no duplicates. History folds into the job's `update` action, keyed by the part's description (`part "X" added` / `part "X"` / `part "X" removed`) rather than its number, since a part's number is no longer stable enough to identify it across edits; a no-op edit (summary unchanged) writes no history row. Each of the three routes returns the job's full, freshly-recomputed part list (`items`, each carrying its own `position`) and `attachmentWarnings` alongside its own result, the same way the whole-job save already does, so a screen acting on the reply never has to separately re-fetch either.

`PUT /jobcards/:id` itself, after Stage 4b, only ever touches the job's own single-value fields (status, priority, due date, description, PO number, previous job, quality level job) plus the invoice-time archive. It takes no `items` and no `assigneeIds` — sending either is simply ignored (an unrecognised body key, same as any other), and the delete-guard against removing a line with logged time now lives solely in `jobcard-items.js`'s own `DELETE` route.

**A repeat job is one that names the previous job it repeats** — there is no separate tick. The Customer Input card's "Previous Job (if repeat)" box (a suggestion list over job numbers) is always shown; filling it in makes the job a repeat, clearing it makes it not one. `POST`/`PUT /jobcards/:id` store `repeat_job_reference` trimmed, empty → null; Statistics counts a repeat by a non-empty reference. The old `is_repeat_job` tick was dropped by `columnDrops.js` after `db/repeatJobFold.js` (pure, tested in `server/test/repeatJobFold.test.js`) folded it: a tick with no previous job named became a "System" comment on its job dated at its creation, and a reference left on an unticked job was cleared. A restored backup that still carries the tick gets the same fold (`backup-helpers.js`). Old trail entries still word `isRepeatJob`.

## Intended, not findings

Each of these was decided (2026-10-14); a review or bug hunt does not raise it.

- **The close-out questions (files, sign-off) are asked twice on a job's way out** — once when it first reaches billing, once when it is archived. Moves within billing (To be Invoiced → Call for Payment) ask neither, but every billing move still has the hard time checks and the PO question.
- **A done job put back on hold counts as live work again** (overdue mark, Statistics live/overdue counts) — the hold is real waiting. Only Action Required is judged by the status it remembers. Its finish date never moves: Statistics dates a job with no logged work by the *first* move into a finished status.
- **"Jobs in active progress" counts jobs set to In Progress plus jobs with a clock running right now**, since status no longer follows work.
- **Status never follows work.** Starting, stopping or logging time, a forgotten clock being cut, or a part being added, changed or removed never moves a job's status. People set every status by hand; a job being worked can read Open until someone moves it (2026-10-27).
- **Action Required drifts through the rainbow and never blinks** — a ~6s colour drift, 24s under reduced motion; never a flash. Its words stay one steady colour.
- **Unarchive returns a job to the status it had just before archiving**, or to Call for Payment for a job archived before statuses were remembered. It never asks.
- **The PO question is asked, never a block, and is asked again on each billing move while the PO number is still empty.** Carrying on is recorded in that move's trail entry.
- **The job list filters by group, not by single status.** Single statuses are filtered on the Search page.
- **Quote references became comments by "System", dated when the job was created**, so they sit at the start of the job's comments. On a job created after the comment-read baseline that comment counts as new for whoever hasn't opened its comments.
- **A converted work entry that recorded only the worker's name reads "for <name>" even when the actor is that same person:** no account was recorded and names are never compared.
- **Parts split from one old Save sit at the same moment and list newest-first like every other tie, with the status move on the original (first-part) entry.** Not a bug.
- **The Activity Log is worded by the same writer as the job History window, plus one for everything else.** Sentences are built in the browser, not stored: a job's entry goes through `describeEntry` (`utils/historySentences.js`) with the job's number added after it; every other kind of record goes through `describeActivity` (`utils/activitySentences.js`), which names the record by its current name (`recordName`, looked up by the server) and falls back to the name the entry itself recorded, then to "a deleted <kind>". Fields are said in plain words ("contact phone", "time zone"), roles as Admin/Manager/Employee, PIN changes as "changed the PIN", failure reasons as "wrong PIN" — never a raw action, snake_case field or stored code. The same writer words the Search page's Activity rows. Because sentences are not stored, the Activity Log's search box matches the stored text (who, job number, record name, changes), not the sentence — typing a status's display name ("In Progress") will not find a move to it. The search box applies on Enter or when it loses focus, never while typing.
- **A damaged trail row is skipped by both the conversion and every History read, and counted in the log;** it is never shown and never fails the window. A skipped row still counts in the activity search's total and page count — a damaged row is a corruption marker to be found in the log, not something to paginate around, so a page one row short is accepted. Do not raise "search counts rows it never shows".
- **The once-only trail conversion reads each row's stored JSON twice** (once to tell damaged from fine, once to convert). It runs once per database, so a second return convention to save the parse is not worth having. Do not raise.
- **A mention record keeps the name as it was typed in the comment** (`mentioned_name`), not the person's current name: it exists to find and highlight that text in the comment, and the comment text itself keeps the old spelling. A rename or the startup name tidy folds a person's *author* name onto their past comments and leaves mention records alone. Do not raise "mentions keep the old name".
- **Marking comments as read writes no trail entry.** `PUT /jobcards/:id/notes/read` is not an edit of the job and would add an entry every time the comments window opened.

- **No shared "write a change and its trail entry" helper.** Every route writes its change and its `recordHistory` entry inside its own explicit `db.transaction`. A wrapper was considered and rejected: it cannot know which other steps (a sign-out, a status follow-up) belong inside, which is the mistake it would be meant to prevent.
- **An old worker entry whose lists can't be read back exactly says "changed who's on the job".** The startup conversion only names the person when the stored lists allow a single answer; it never guesses, and the worker's account can't be recovered for old entries (2026-10-15, bug log Round 6).
- **A part change that moves the job's status words the move as a plain follow-up** ("The job moved from Done to In Progress") under the part line, filed under Job details, not Status — the person changed the part, not the status (2026-10-15).
- **The first trail entry of a job words its workers like every later one** (`assigneeNames`, `from: 'none'`), read back from the rows the create just wrote.
- **Answering a mention writes no trail entry.** It is a side effect of the person's own comment, which already has its entry.
- **A mention stays answered even if the answering comment is later deleted.** The answer is the fact that the person replied; the deletion does not reopen it.
- **Deleting the comment that asked a question drops the question with it, silently.** Once the comment is gone nobody is asking anything, so there is nothing left to answer or flag; the deletion's own trail entry is enough.
- **The @name in an old comment is not rewritten when the person is renamed.** The comment keeps what was typed, as every comment's author name used to before the rename sync.
- **An archived (deactivated) person's open mentions are left as they are** and reappear if the account is reactivated.
- **Open mentions on invoiced/archived jobs are hidden, not answered.** They are not counted or listed; unarchiving the job brings them back.
- **The mentions section waits only for open windows.** A page with its own unsaved form (not a window) can be covered by it; what was typed stays underneath.
- **A mention arriving while the person is in that same job's comments and replies there never shows a row.** The reply answers it before the list is read again.

Mentions — decided with the owner (2026-10-15); a review or bug hunt does not raise these either:

- **Only the person's own reply clears a mention.** Nobody — not the office, not an admin — can mark it dealt with for them; a question answered in person still gets a typed reply ("sorted in person").
- **No ready-made replies.** No quick-reply buttons or suggested answers: the person types what they mean, and any comment they send counts.
- **Anyone active can be mentioned**, not only the people on the job.
- **Admins get the window too.** Same rule for every role.
- **Mentions are live, not sign-in only.** The list appears while signed in and keeps itself up to date, because admins are never signed out for inactivity and would otherwise not hear about a question for days.
- **Blocking, with Sign out as the only exit.** Someone with several questions waiting replies to every one before carrying on; that is intended.
- **One window, clock first.** The forgotten-clock question and the mention rows share one window; the clock is always answered first (it affects pay and billing), mention rows stay greyed until it is.
- **Mentions wait for open windows; the clock does not.** Chosen over interrupting at once: a question never lands on someone mid-way through a job screen.
